question.text: Martyrs and people who perform one miracle can receive this recognition, after which they earn the title of "blessed."
question.clue: By what name is this process, which implies that the recipients are "blessed" by Heaven, called?

swap.leadin: Name some noteworthy popes of the Catholic Church.
swap.text: This pope called for the First Crusade and offered a remission of sins for those who would participate in it.
swap.answerHtml: Pope Urban II [accept Odo of Chatillon or Otho de Lagery; prompt on Urban]
swap.clue: This pope allied himself with Roger I of Sicily, and he was heavily influenced by a delegation sent by Alexius I Komnenos.

question.leadin: Pope Clement V issued the bull Vox in excelso to dissolve this organization.
question.text: Name this organization that was accused of apostasy, idolatry, and sodomy by the church. Philip IV of France killed most members of this organization, including its leader Jacques de Molay.
question.clue: At the Battle of Montgisard, they helped defeat Saladin's army, and they were founded after the First Crusade by Hugues de Payens and Godfrey de Saint-Omer to protect pilgrims traveling to the Holy Land.

swap.text: An Armenian ruler with this name known as the "Illuminator" was responsible for converting the Armeniansfrom Zoroastrianism to Christianity. The first pope with this name names a series of "chants" while the thirteenthnames a calendar which replaced the Julian.
swap.clue: Those two theologians with this name are from Nyssa and Nazianzus, and are considered "Cappadocian fathers" along with Basil the Great.

question.leadin: This council was preceded by a failed attempt at Pisa.
question.text: Name this church council that ended the Western Schism and burned Jan Hus burned at the stake for promoting Utraquism. Much to the ire of Martin V and other popes, it declared that future councils should meet every 10 years.
question.clue: Other decisions included the canonization of St. Bridget of Sweden and a voting of special privilege to Emperor Sigismund, who had called this meeting.

swap.text: The Society of Jesus was formally made part of the Catholic Church in 1540 by this pope, who also convened the Council of Trent.
swap.clue: This pope who assembled the Holy League decisively defeated by the Ottomans at the Battle of Preveza.

question.leadin: Catherine of Siena unsuccessfully appealed to one leader in this city to relocate.
question.text: Name this city, where a rival papacy was established during the Western Schism. Petrarch ["pet-rark"] compared this city's eponymous papacy to the Babylonian Captivity.
question.clue: This city was called "a sewer where all the muck of the universe collects" by Petrarch, who coined an enduring Biblical nickname for it.

swap.text: During his leadership, Salazar maintained close relations with this religious institution via the Concordat of 1940. With the Lateran Treaty of 1929, this institution gained a state of its own in Vatican City.
swap.clue: Ludwig Windthorst led a party supporting this organization that was named for its seating location in the parliament, the Center Party.

question.leadin: Identify the following about some popes named Clement.
question.text: Clement XIV abolished this religious order in 1773. This order was founded by Ignatius of Loyola and was a key force in the Counter-Reformation.
question.clue: Two members of this group prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk and another created a lunisolar calendar for the last Ming emperor.

swap.leadin: It resulted in the election of the Swiss Antipope Clement VII.
swap.text: Identify this period in which Philip IV of France moved the Papacy to Avignon, named after a duration of time in the Old Testament.
swap.clue: This term which also applies to an exile of Jews from Judah begun by Nebuchadnezzar and ended by Cyrus the Great.

question.leadin: Terrorists planned to assassinate this pope during a visit to the Philippines in the first phase of the Bojinka Plot.
question.text: Name this pope who established World Youth Day in 1985. This pope's visit to his home country motivated the formation of the Solidarity movement, which went on to end communist rule in that country.
question.clue: This man made a prison visit to forgive Mehmet Ali Agca, a member of the Grey Wolves who tried to kill him.

swap.leadin: This concept was made Catholic dogma in 1870.
swap.text: What is the two-word name in English for the idea that the pope speaks for the whole church and cannot be in error?
swap.clue: This doctrine under which, in certain matters, the pope is free from error.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the year 1968.
question.text: In July, this pope issued the encyclical Humanae vitae, which condemned artificial birth control. In 1968, this pope who closed the Second Vatican Council also beatified the Korean Martyrs.
question.answerHtml: Paul VI (or Giovanni Battista Enrico Antonio Maria Montini)
question.clue: This pope who canonized the Uganda martyrs and later visited Kampala in 1969 in the first papal trip to Africa. This pope presided over the end of Vatican II after the death of John XXIII ("the twenty-third").

swap.text: This pope was the best-known advocate of Lublin Thomism, which he learned at the Catholic University of Lublin in his native Poland. He denounced abortion and capital punishment in Evangelium Vitae.
swap.answerHtml: John Paul II [or Karol Wojtyla; or Ioannes Paulus II; or Giovanni Paolo II; or Jan Paweł II; prompt on any of the aforementioned names that do not include "the second"; do not accept or prompt on answers with just "John" or "Paul"]
swap.clue: This man survived an assassination attempt by the Turkish Mehmet Ali Agca, whom he later forgave.

question.leadin: This order was founded by Gerard after the First Crusade, about a century before the Knights Templar.
question.text: Name this order of knights which was originally founded to heal injured pilgrims.
question.answerHtml: Knights Hospitaller [accept Knights of Malta, but do not read this answer aloud]
question.clue: This group was founded by merchants from Amalfi, and was later led by Gerard Thom.

swap.leadin: This event was caused by the election of Pope Urban VI and the accusations of intimidation which led to his election.
swap.text: Name this event, during which there were two or three claimants to the Papacy, residing in Rome, France and, for a brief period, Pisa. This event is sometimes described as "great", causing confusion with a separate event of 1054.
swap.answerHtml: The Western Schism [accept Great Divide or Great Occidental Schism or Schism of 1378 or Great Western Schism, do not accept or prompt on “Great Schism” or “Schism”]
swap.clue: Pierre d'Ailly ("dah-YEE") and Jean Gerson ("zhawn zhair-SON") promoted a conciliar resolution to this conflict, which began when 13 rebels staged an election in Fondi ("FOHN-dee") with regalia stolen by a camerlengo.

question.leadin: In 1303 armed forces of Philip IV stormed into the pope's residence and took him prisoner with the help of a powerful Italian noble, who reputedly slapped the pope in the face.
question.text: Identify this event, named for the town in which the pope was imprisoned for three days.

swap.text: The seizure of this six-year-old from his Jewish parents on Pius IX's watch, on the rumor that he had been baptized by his nanny, became a cause celebre for opponents of Papal rule.

question.text: This first pope of the Captivity promulgated a crusade at the Council of Vienne and also proposed a Franco-Mongolian alliance against those durn Muzzlums.
question.clue: He rescinded an earlier papal bull which proclaimed that outside of the church, there is no salvation.

swap.text: The last Merovingian king, Childeric III, was tonsured after this pope helped overthrow him.
